Ratifying 28 and leaving the digest at '17-24, 26 and 27' would make the protocol file stale about the protocol, which is convention 24's failure mode in the worst possible place. The same call was made and recorded in ARCH-20260922-001.

questions_for_advisor: NOTHING GUARDS THE PRECEDENCE CLAIM. A pre-registration's whole value is that it preceded the run, and today that is provable only because I compared a commit's author date to a trace header by hand. No test does it. A guard could: for each docs/preregistration-*.md with a matching committed trace, assert the prereg's authoring commit predates the trace's written_at. It would have to tolerate rebases, which rewrite committer dates but not author dates. This is Convention 28 pointed at the protocol itself, and I have not written it because it is a new guard rather than a repair of a broken one.

B19's row deliberately does not name a cause, because the stdout does not distinguish the two candidates and ARCH-20260922-021's own constraints forbid fixing an unobserved cause. If the sweep cap is per SESSION rather than per unit, a repeat of 2 legitimately stops after one, B19 is a message defect rather than an arithmetic one, and it is medium at most. That reading should be settled from the code before -021 writes anything.

§33.3 records that escalation took 70% of the spend, which is the second time in one day the invisible tier turned out to be where the money went. Combined with §6.10's 70-78%, that is now three independent observations of the same share on a tier with no ledger row. It may be worth promoting from 'a gap in the ledger' to a measured fact in §6 in its own right — but that is a ruling about what §6 asserts, not an instrument repair.
